label: Ripples
idea: One comma per tile with the bands at equal distance from its outline: a light moat (0.36 comma radii), a dark ring (0.135), and further bands only where the comma's cell is deep. The cell is the comma's Voronoi cell among its copies, so neighbours meet band to band; a 0.05 light channel on the cell border keeps copies apart and a light pool lies where cells meet. find() is a rule with no per-group table: (1) the default tile, or without presets the Dirichlet tile of the point farthest from its copies; (2) a linear map the point group allows that makes the tile at most 1.25 times longer than wide (cap 2.4), so strips get a stretched comma and stretched bands; (3) a small linear program fits the largest comma over 72 turns and three stretches, on three candidate seats (the tile; a half-ringed strip for *x; the roomiest place of the tile with the comma kept inside it); (4) exact distances on a grid in the comma's own frame, an opening of radius 0.02, marching squares. Verified: all 17 on the mini's sheet (dark 0.516-0.583, bare 0.208-0.430, solid 0.250-0.339, overlap 0, 497-618 vertices, 13-52 ms); src/shapes.js validateShapes passes all 17 with presets and carried; copies keep 0.050 apart; a turned, scaled, shifted group without presets gets the turned motif to 2e-12 tile sizes; 69 off-page lattices give no error and no overlap (one has bare 0.464). The sand side reads. Not verified: the real page (3D fold, 60 px tiles, phone), since nothing is integrated.
hint: a comma and its echoes: bands at equal distance from it, out to the next comma
weaknesses: No hard rule is broken and no target of (b) is missed on the sheet, but bare reaches 0.43 against the 0.45 target (*632 0.430, *333 and 4*2 0.429); without presets it is 0.436.

The comma itself is smaller than the page's: 10-17 % of the tile against 30 %, 0.57-0.97 tile sizes long. What fills the tile is the comma with its ring, and the light moat is what the eye reads first.
Six cells are not the default tile (333, 22*, 442, 632, 3*3, 4*2). The tile holds the whole comma and moat, but the ring is cut by the tile edge and slices of neighbours' rings lie in the tile.

In o, **, xx, 22*, 2*22 and *x the bands are at equal distance only in a stretched metric: comma and bands are stretched 1.8 to 2.9 times, and a band is up to 2.4 times wider along the tile than across it.
In *x the ring is open on the side of the comma's back: the strip is 0.43 wide and a full ring left a comma 0.19 across.

Thin corners are busier than the rest: 12 petals plus an arc band round the 6-fold corner of *632, 8 petals at the 4-fold corners of *442, 6 small petals (0.036 tile areas each) at the 6-fold centres of 632.

Corners of one cell can differ in kind (*333: petals at two corners, a swollen ring and pool at the third). The kinds and the seat flip at thresholds, so a small lattice change can change the picture.
Without presets the motif is a different one wherever the default tile is not the group's roomiest tile (22x, 22*, 2*22, 632, 3*3, 4*2 most visibly). Both versions pass every check.

Band-to-band meeting across a channel is exact for moat and ring. For deep-corner bands it holds at rotation centres and mirror corners only; two different corners meeting at a generic vertex are not reconciled.
The sheet's dark number for *442 (0.583) is the kit's lattice-aligned sampling running along the channels; by polygon area it is 0.563.
The ring's neck is 0.055 at its thinnest, and round corners (radius 0.02) have only three or four vertices each.
The msMax of 52 is from the final sheet run; other runs of the same code on the mini reached 68 ms for o. In node on the Intel it is 35-100 ms.
My own lab/check.mjs reported a false self-crossing on collinear channel edges in *333; I fixed the checker, and the production validator never flagged it.
